title: Height Resolution Order Tracer
description: A folder tree of one MicroSim and four numbered height sources: the // CANVAS_HEIGHT comment in the script, canvasHeight in metadata.json, a CANVAS_HEIGHT comment in main.html, and computed drawHeight + controlHeight. The learner toggles sources, edits their values, predicts the winner, and presses Trace to see which source sync-iframe-heights.py would use and the resulting iframe height, CANVAS_HEIGHT + 2.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Web Development
MicroSim Engineering
Iframe Heights

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will examine a MicroSim folder and determine which of the four height sources a synchronization tool would use, and what iframe height results.
prerequisites: The CANVAS_HEIGHT comment and the rule iframe height = CANVAS_HEIGHT + 2 (Chapter 12)
The files in a MicroSim folder: main.html, the script, metadata.json, index.md (Chapter 2)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

controls.label: Trace
controls.action: Walk the sources from priority 1 and stop at the first value

assumptions: The folder is named demo-sim and the script is demo-sim.js, so the tool looks for demo-sim.js.
limitations: The graphHeight term, the canvasHeight-variable and createCanvas() fallbacks of source 4 are described in the text but not modeled.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then trace, on varied folder configurations
keyQuestions: Which source does the tool read first, and when does it stop?
What happens to a lower source that disagrees?
Why does the tool write the comment back after using source 4?
commonMisconceptions: The tool takes the largest or the most recent height it finds.
A stale value in metadata.json is harmless only because it is ignored; it will drift and mislead readers of the file.
An iframe with no height found is set to a default height.
assessmentOpportunities: Given a description of a MicroSim folder, the learner names the source the tool uses and the iframe height it writes.
The learner explains why a lower-priority value that disagrees is never read, and how to remove the drift.
